content: This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication regularly for an extended period, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., magnesium blood levels, vitamin B-12 levels) may be conducted to monitor your condition and check for side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture. Do not open the packets until you are ready to use the medication. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: Before starting esomeprazole, read the Medication Guide and, if available, the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually once daily, at least one hour before a meal. This medication may also be administered through a nasogastric or gastric tube. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For 5-milligram strength packets, empty the contents into a container with 1 teaspoon (5 milliliters) of water. Stir the mixture well and let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes to thicken. Stir again and drink the entire mixture within 30 minutes. For other strengths, mix the packet contents with 1 tablespoon (15 milliliters) of water, stir, let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes, stir again, and drink within 30 minutes. Do not crush or chew the medication granules. Antacids may be taken alongside this medication if needed. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache or abdominal pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), such as esomeprazole, may rarely cause vitamin B-12 deficiency, especially if taken daily for a prolonged period (three years or longer). Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, particularly bone loss and fractures, as well as C. difficile-associated diarrhea. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you notice symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking esomeprazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other PPIs (e.g., lansoprazole, omeprazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Some symptoms may actually be signs of a more serious condition. PPIs, including esomeprazole, may increase the risk of bone fractures, particularly with long-term use, higher doses, and in older adults. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. However, similar drugs do pass into breast milk, and the effects on a nursing infant are unknown. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products require stomach acid for proper absorption. Esomeprazole decreases stomach acid, which may affect how well these products work. Esomeprazole is very similar to omeprazole. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If your doctor instructs you to use this medication regularly for a long time, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., magnesium blood levels, vitamin B-12 levels) may be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments.
